title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in neurology: biomarkers and clinical implications
title_zh: 线粒体功能障碍在神经学中的生物标志物与临床意义
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a shared downstream pathogenic mechanism across a wide spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from primary mitochondrial diseases to conditions including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, hereditary ataxias and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. This Review examines the role of mitochondrial biomarkers in improving diagnostic accuracy, patient stratification and monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response. Primary mitochondrial diseases are presented as proof-of-concept models of impaired oxidative phosphorylation, providing a framework for biomarker identification and validation with translational relevance to other neurological diseases. Mitochondrial biomarkers can be broadly categorized into four domains: fluid biomarkers, reflecting metabolic alterations and stress signalling; genetic biomarkers, capturing mitochondrial DNA integrity and dynamics; multi-omics approaches, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures; and imaging biomarkers, enabling in vivo assessment of structural and functional consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. Across disorders, these biomarkers reveal shared disturbances in bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial genome maintenance and inflammatory signalling. However, clinical implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, biological variability and reduced disease specificity. Integrated, multimodal biomarker strategies, combined with longitudinal validation, will be essential for supporting precision medicine and guiding the development of therapies to target mitochondrial pathways in neurology. Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a convergent downstream pathogenic process across many neurological disorders. This Review evaluates how mitochondrial biomarkers can enhance diagnostic accuracy, support patient stratification and enable monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response.
abstract_zh: 线粒体功能障碍正被越来越多地认定为涵盖广泛神经系统疾病谱的共同下游致病机制，从原发性线粒体疾病到包括肌萎缩侧索硬化、阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病、多发性硬化症、遗传性共济失调和特发性炎症性肌病在内的疾病。本综述探讨了线粒体生物标志物在提高诊断准确性、患者分层以及监测疾病进展和治疗反应中的作用。原发性线粒体疾病被作为受损氧化磷酸化的概念模型进行介绍，为生物标志物的鉴定和验证提供了具有转化意义的框架，其框架在其他神经系统疾病中均具可转化性。线粒体生物标志物可大致分为四大类：体液生物标志物，反映代谢改变和应激信号；遗传生物标志物，捕捉线粒体DNA的完整性和动力学；多组学方法，整合转录组、蛋白质组和代谢组特征；以及成像生物标志物，实现对线粒体功能障碍在体内结构和功能后果的评估。在各种疾病中，这些生物标志物揭示了生物能、氧化还原稳态、线粒体基因组维持和炎症信号方面的共同紊乱。然而，临床应用受到方法学异质性、生物学变异性和疾病特异性降低的限制。综合的、多模式的生物标志物策略，结合纵向验证，对于支持精准医疗和指导针对神经学中线粒体途径的治疗开发至关重要。线粒体功能障碍正被越来越多地认定为许多神经系统疾病的汇聚下游致病过程。本综述评估了线粒体生物标志物如何增强诊断准确性，支持患者分层，并实现对疾病进展和治疗反应的监测。
